'''Tomoko M. Nakanishi''' (中西友子) is a Japanese [[Chemist|chemical scientist]] leading in the development and application of [[Imaging|imaging techniques]] using [[radiation]] and [[radionuclide]]s for research on water and element [[Plant physiology|physiology in plants]]. Her research strategy excels by optimizing a variety of complementary radiochemical/nuclear analytical techniques together with innovative experimental set-ups to get insight in a part of the [[plant physiology]].

== Early life and education ==
Nakanishi was born in 1950 in [[Kanazawa]], [[Ishikawa Prefecture|Ishikawa]], Japan as third child.<ref>{{Cite book |title=My Life: Twenty Japanese Women Scientists |publisher=Uchida Rokakuho |year=2001 |isbn=978-4753661817 |location=Tokyo, Japan |publication-date=2001-01-01}}</ref> Her father was a medical doctor in practice.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2020-05-14 |title=【研究者の肖像Vol23】とにかく"現場"に足を運ぶ。対象と素直に向き合う。それが"定説"を覆すことも。どんな研究でも、その姿勢が大事 中西友子 - Technologist's magazine |url=https://technologist.high-five.careers/2020/05/14/post-6241/ |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=technologist.high-five.careers |language=ja}}</ref> She grew up in Tokyo and graduated high school in 1969 from highschool attached to the [[Tokyo University of Education]] when the [[student movement]] was at the highest in Japan.<ref name=":0" />

After graduated from [[Rikkyo University|St. Paul's university]], very close to her house in 1973, she started her research carrier at the [[University of Tokyo]] in [[radiochemistry]], supervised by Masatake Honda in 1973.<ref name=":0" /> She earned her Ph.D. by determining the half-lives of long lived radioactive nuclides, <sup>92</sup>Nb and <sup>91</sup>Nb for the first time in 1978.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Chatt |first1=A. |date=2017 |title=Laudation for Professor Tomoko Nakanishi: 2016 Hevesy Medal Awardee |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10967-016-5129-2 |journal=J Radioanal Nucl Chem |volume=311 |issue=2 |pages=945–946 |bibcode=2017JRNC..311..945C |doi=10.1007/s10967-016-5129-2}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=私と放射線・RIとの長い系譜 |url=https://www.jrias.or.jp/pdf/2306_RIREKISYO_NAKANISHI.pdf |website=Isotope News 2023年6月号 No.787 |language=Ja}}</ref>

Then she found her job at Zeon Co., 8 years before the [[Equal Employment Opportunity Law (Japan)|Equal Employment Opportunity Law]] came into force in Japan.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Dinner Speech: Agricultural Implications of the Fukushima Nuclear Accident |url=https://www.naefrontiers.org/43606/Dinner-Speech-Agricultural-Implications-of-the-Fukushima-Nuclear-Accident?source=generalSearch |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=www.naefrontiers.org}}</ref> There she had to change her research field to [[plant physiology]] to initiate biology group.<ref name=":0" /> She could start her plant physiology work in chemical biodynamics lab. at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Laurence Berkeley Laboratory]], in [[University of California|Univ. of California]] for about 2 years.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /> She also learned about [[plant tissue culture]] work directly from Prof. [[Toshio Murashige]], who was a world premiere plant scientist in [[University of California, Davis|Davis, Univ. of California]].<ref name=":0" /> Back to the company she established plant research laboratory, aiming to collect the fragrance produced from the automatic tissue culture system.<ref name=":0" />

Then she was offered an assistant position in the Agricultural Dept. of [[University of Tokyo|the University of Tokyo]] in 1987.<ref name=":0" /> Moving to the university, she had to set up her own environment for the research by herself and utilized the reactor or an accelerator in [[Japan Atomic Energy Agency|JAEA (Japan Atomic Energy Agency)]] and [[National Institute of Radiological Sciences|NIRS (National Institute of Radiological Sciences)]] for plant research.<ref name=":3" />

== Carrier and Research ==
She began to apply [[Radiochemistry|radiochemical method]] for [[plant physiology]], due to lack of any report regarding introduction of various radiochemical methods to plant physiology and to find out how many new activities the living plant showed.<ref name=":2" /> Her research is the first to truly combine [[radiochemistry]] and plant physiology.<ref name=":4">{{Cite book |last=Nakanishi |first=Tomoko M. |date=2021 |title=Novel Plant Imaging and Analysis |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-33-4992-6 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-981-33-4992-6|isbn=978-981-33-4991-9 }}</ref>

In the case of [[water]], she measured the small amount of water actually moving inside the [[plant]].<ref name=":2" /> Using both [[Oxygen-15 labelled water|<sup>15</sup>O]] (half-life: 2 min) and [[Tritium|<sup>3</sup>H]] to follow the movement of water, she found the circulation of water in the [[Plant stem|stem]] for the first time.<ref name=":4" /> She also introduced [[neutron]] [[Imaging|imaging method]] for analyzing water in the living plant, where she found there was not direct contact of water on the surface of the [[root]] growing in soil, suggesting the root was not absorbing water solution but [[water vapor]].<ref name=":4" /> She was also questioned about metal absorption in soil, whether metal solution or metal vapor. To solve these unanswered problem, she stressed the importance of plant research growing in soil, not only in [[Hydroponics|water culture]]<ref name=":4" />

She has developed the [[Macroscopic scale|macroscopic]] and [[Microscopic scale|microscopic]] real-time [[Radionuclide|radioisotope]] imaging system.<ref name=":2" /> She imaged physiological processes [[in situ]] using radioisotopes of seventeen elements so far, including the gas movement, how plants fix <sup>14</sup>CO<sub>2</sub> gas and where metabolites go to create new plant tissue.<ref name=":4" />

As tools for studying the essential elements [[magnesium]] and [[potassium]], she developed an effective production and separation techniques: alpha bombardment of aluminum followed by radiochemical purification of <sup>28</sup>Mg, and milking of <sup>42</sup>K from radioactive <sup>42</sup>Ar gas, and used these tracers for plant study for the first time.<ref name=":4" />

After [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake]], her group has led studies of the agricultural consequences of radioactive contamination from [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]].<ref name=":2" /> In addition to numerous publications in the periodical literature and conference proceedings, she has edited four books on this topic, published in 2013,<ref name=":5">{{Cite book |date=2013 |editor-last=Nakanishi |editor-first=Tomoko M. |editor2-last=Tanoi |editor2-first=Keitaro |title=Agricultural Implications of the Fukushima Nuclear Accident |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-4-431-54328-2  |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-4-431-54328-2|isbn=978-4-431-54327-5 }}</ref> 2016,<ref name=":6">{{Cite book |date=2016 |editor-last=Nakanishi |editor-first=Tomoko M. |editor2-last=Tanoi |editor2-first=Keitaro |title=Agricultural Implications of the Fukushima Nuclear Accident |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-4-431-55828-6 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-4-431-55828-6|isbn=978-4-431-55826-2 |hdl=2078/ebook:82593 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> 2019<ref name=":7">{{Cite book |date=2019 |editor-last=Nakanishi |editor-first=Tomoko M. |editor2-last=O`Brien |editor2-first=Martin |editor3-last=Tanoi |editor3-first=Keitaro |title=Agricultural Implications of the Fukushima Nuclear Accident (III) |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-13-3218-0 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-981-13-3218-0|isbn=978-981-13-3217-3 }}</ref> and 2023<ref name=":8">{{Cite book |date=2023 |editor-last=Nakanishi |editor-first=Tomoko M. |editor2-last=Tanoi |editor2-first=Keitaro |title=Agricultural Implications of Fukushima Nuclear Accident (IV) |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-19-9361-9 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-981-19-9361-9|isbn=978-981-19-9360-2 |doi-access=free }}</ref> by [[Springer Nature|Springer]]. The online version has been accessed more than 213,000,<ref name=":5" /> 151, 000,<ref name=":6" /> 103,000<ref name=":7" /> and 30,000<ref name=":8" /> times for the first, second, third and fourth book, respectively.

She was appointed as a professor in Graduate School of Agricultural and Life Sciences in [[University of Tokyo|the University of Tokyo]] in 2001.<ref name=":3" /> Retired from the University of Tokyo she was appointed as a [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=平成２８年度 東京大学名誉教授 |url=https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/content/400042744.pdf |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=The University of Tokyo |page=2 |language=Ja}}</ref> Then she got an offer as a president of [[Hoshi University]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=星薬科大學報 第89号 |url=https://www.hoshi.ac.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/no89.pdf |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Hoshi University |page=3 |language=Ja}}</ref> Retired from Hoshi University she was appointed as a professor emeritus of Hoshi University in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=令和5（2023）年度事業報告書 |url=https://www.hoshi.ac.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/2023_jigyohokoku_hojin.pdf |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Hoshi University |page=12 |language=Ja}}</ref> She was offered an Auditor of Fukushima Institute for Research, Education and Innovation in 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fukushima Institute for Research, Education and Innovation (F-REI) |title=Institute Information｜Fukushima Institute for Research, Education and Innovation (F-REI) |url=https://www.f-rei.go.jp/english/institution/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250216093335/https://www.f-rei.go.jp/english/institution |archive-date=2025-02-16 |access-date=2025-05-04 |work=Fukushima Institute for Research, Education and Innovation (F-REI) |language=en}}</ref>

Nakanishi was a council member of [[Science Council of Japan]], a commissioner of [[Japanese Atomic Energy Commission|Japan Atomic Energy Commission]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=ー歴代原子力委員ー |url=https://www.aec.go.jp/about/iin/iin.pdf |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Japan Atomic Energy Commission |language=Ja}}</ref> a vice president of Engineering Academy of Japan,<ref>{{Cite web |title=日本工学アカデミー３０年史 |url=https://www.eaj.or.jp/eajlocal/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/EAJ-30th-anniversary-magazine.pdf |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=The Engineering Academy of Japan |page=92 |language=Ja}}</ref> a president of The Japan Soc. of Nuclear and Radiochemical Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |title=学会について |url=http://www.radiochem.org/community/president.html |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=The Japan Society of Nuclear and Radiochemical Sciences |language=Ja}}</ref> and a commissioner of Japanese National Commission for [[UNESCO]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=日本ユネスコ国内委員会委員名簿（平成２３年７月２３日現在） |url=https://warp.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/8431033/www.mext.go.jp/component/a_menu/other/micro_detail/__icsFiles/afieldfile/2011/10/11/1311937_002.pdf |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=National Diet Library, Japan |language=Ja}}</ref> She is now a vice president of Agricultural Academy of Japan,<ref>{{Cite web |title=日本農学アカデミー会員名簿 |url=https://www.academy-nougaku.jp/member.html |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=The Agricultural Academy of Japan |language=Ja}}</ref> an Administrative Council of [[Kyoto University]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-12 |title=運営方針委員の任命について |url=https://www.kyoto-u.ac.jp/ja/news/2024-12-12-1 |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=京都大学 |language=ja}}</ref> Board of Trustees Member of [[Chubu University]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=学校法人中部大学 |title=役員・評議員一覧 {{!}} 学園概要 |url=https://www.chubu.jp/about/officer/ |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=学校法人中部大学 |language=ja}}</ref> etc.

== Awards and honors ==
Nakanishi is a conspicuous and influential role model for Japanese women, having been awarded the [[Saruhashi Prize]] in 2000 as the nation's outstanding woman in science.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-06 |title=受賞者一覧 |url=https://saruhashisho.wordpress.com/list/ |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=猿橋賞 |language=ja}}</ref> She received Contribution Award from Atomic Energy Society of Japan in 2001, and Society Award of Nuclear and Radiochemical Sciences in Japan in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=歴代の学会賞／奨励賞の受賞者と受賞テーマ |url=http://www.radiochem.org/community/commendation.html |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=The Japan Society of Nuclear and Radiochemical Sciences |language=Ja}}</ref>

Her contributions to science and to society have been recognized internationally, notably by Hevesy Medal Award, selecting one premiere radiochemist every year, named after a Nobel Prize Laurie, Dr. G. Hevesy, in 2016.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded [[Ordre national du Mérite|the Ordre national du Mérite]] in 2013<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remise de l'Ordre national du Mérite au Professeur Tomoko Nakanishi |url=https://jp.ambafrance.org/Remise-de-l-Ordre-national-du-7704 |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=French Embassy in Tokyo |language=Fr}}</ref> as well as [[Ordre des Palmes académiques]] in 2022<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remise des Palmes académiques à la Professeure Tomoko Nakanishi |url=https://jp.ambafrance.org/Remise-des-Palmes-academiques-a-la-Professeure-Tomoko-Nakanishi |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=French Embassy in Tokyo |language=Fr}}</ref> from French government. She was also awarded the Göteborg Lise Meitner Award in 2025 as the first Japanese scientist.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-30 |title=Gothenburg Lise Meitner Award |url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/departments/physics/resources-and-collaborations/gpc/gothenburg-lise-meitner-award/ |access-date=2025-05-04 |website=www.chalmers.se |language=en}}</ref>

She was elected as a Foreign Member of [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences|the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering]] in 2015<ref>{{Cite web |year=2016 |title=JSPS Stockholm Newsletter English Edition Vol. 23 |url=https://www.jsps-sto.com/wp-content/uploads/Newsletter/en/English-NL-23.pdf |page=22}}</ref> and [[Royal Society of Arts and Sciences in Gothenburg|the Royal Society of Arts and Sciences in Göteborg]] in 2017,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Birger Karlsson |title=KVVS The Royal Society of Arts and Sciences in Gothenburg-Entering the 21st century. |publisher=Göteborg |year=2016 |isbn=978-9198042078}}</ref> and an Honorary Doctor of [[Chalmers University of Technology]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JSPS STOCKHOLM 2019│ VOL.36 │ 28 |url=https://www.jsps-sto.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/English-Newsletter-Vol.-36.pdf}}</ref>
